findings.title: Upsampled count sums the wrong field and does not invert sample rate
findings.body: transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling rewrites count() to upsampled_count(), and the new SnQL function is sum(sample_weight) cast to int. The only ingest change, _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling, writes contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate onto sample_rate and never sets sample_weight. A client_sample_rate of 0.1 means the stored event represents about 10 events, but nothing computes 1/sample_rate, and the aggregate does not read sample_rate. Allowlisted error stats will either query a missing/zero sample_weight column (query error or a count of 0) or, if that column happens to hold the rate, return a fractional rate instead of an upsampled count. The new stats test expects count == 10 for one event at rate 0.1, which this path cannot produce.

findings.title: Error-query detection is a substring match and treats exclusions as errors
findings.body: _is_error_focused_query lowercases the raw query string and returns true if it contains the substring "event.type:error". That also matches negated or unrelated clauses such as "!event.type:error" and "event.type:error OR event.type:transaction". Discover queries that exclude errors are then rewritten from count() to upsampled_count()/sum(sample_weight). Transactions and other non-error events do not have that column, so those stats requests fail or return inflated/zero counts. The same check misses the dashboard errors split, which uses "!event.type:transaction" rather than "event.type:error", so genuine error-only discover queries are not upsampled.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility uses the request dataset, not the dataset actually queried
findings.body: _get_event_stats decides upsampling with the closed-over dataset from get_dataset(request), then runs the query on scoped_dataset. Dashboard widget splitting calls this with discover (and an errors-only or transactions-only query) while the outer dataset is still metrics_performance or metrics_enhanced_performance. _should_apply_sample_weight_transform returns false for those metrics datasets, so the errors split never rewrites count(). The opposite also holds: an errors/discover request dataset can rewrite columns on a scoped dataset that is not the errors dataset. Counts for split dashboard widgets will be wrong or the rewritten function will be invalid on the dataset that actually runs.

findings.title: upsampled_count is only registered on the discover dataset
findings.body: The new upsampled_count SnQL function is added only inside DiscoverDataset.function_converter. is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects returns true for the errors dataset with no query check, and the endpoint then sends yAxis/selected_columns of "upsampled_count() as count" to that dataset. Unless the errors dataset shares this exact converter, allowlisted errors-dataset stats queries will fail function resolution instead of returning an upsampled count. The integration tests only hit discover via event.type:error and do not cover dataset=errors.

findings.title: Allowlist cache key is process-local and invalidation is never called
findings.body: The eligibility cache key is built with hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids))). Tuple hashing is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so workers do not share keys and invalidate_upsampling_cache deletes a different key than the one another process wrote. That helper is also never called when issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist changes, despite the docstring saying it must be. A False or True allowlist result is then reused for 60 seconds. After an allowlist change, stats keep using the old decision: either counts stay un-upsampled or count() is rewritten to sum(sample_weight) for projects that are no longer allowlisted. The new stats tests patch options.get but not the cache, so a later case with the same project ids can still see the first case's cached True and fail or pass for the wrong reason.

findings.title: Accidental gitlink pins a nested copy of the repository
findings.body: This change adds a gitlink/submodule named sentry-repo whose commit is the PR base (a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a). It is unrelated to error upsampling. Checking out the branch will try to materialize a nested repository (or fail if the gitlink has no .gitmodules URL), and it should not be merged.
